the Mg reduction process is a simple and efficient method to produce a mesoporous Si material, which can be used as anode material in Li-ion battery.

the Mg-driven reduction process is an interesting alternative to prepare mesoporous silicon/carbon composite material, and that it is an easy and effective way to obtain a promising anode material for lithium-ion battery.

The main takeaway from our work is that

magnesium-driven reduction reaction of SBA-15 silica template, followed by carbon coating, is a simple, low-cost, scalable process that allows to obtain a mesoporous Si-C composite anode material with high electrochemical performances.

the ‘one spot’ Mg reduction process is a simple and versatile method that allows to obtain mesoporous silicon-based anodic material for high capacity lithium battery with a very good electrochemical performance and reversibility.

the ‘one spot’ reduction of mesoporous silica by Mg is a simple method to obtain mesoporous Si with a very good surface area and pore volume and a very good electrochemical performance when used in a lithium battery.
